Project 02, cultural

Reading Room

All projects

One tall room for a village library. The roof is raked toward the north and cut with narrow slots, so the light arrives high, even and without glare.

Cover
Type
Cultural
Setting
The edge of a village green
Scope
New hall, shelving and furniture
Drawings
Plan, cross section
Status
Concept study

A library needs one thing above all: light you can read by all day.

The room is a plain rectangle, longer than it is wide, with books along both long walls and tables down the middle. Everything that makes it a library is furniture; everything that makes it a building is the roof.

That roof rises toward the north and is cut with a row of narrow slots. Direct sun never reaches the tables, but the room is bright from morning to evening, and the slots throw slow bars of light across the floor as the day turns.

A low porch on the green side gives the village a place to wait, meet and leave bicycles without disturbing the readers inside.
